question: Holding E8's design fixed, how do native utility and attack success of each arm change across open-weight checkpoints of different size and family?

base_plan.rule: every field of the base plan applies unchanged except agent.checkpoint and agent.checkpoint_sha256; the per-checkpoint plan files under fixtures/v6/e2/ are generated mechanically from the base plan and this file

reference_checkpoint: Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF is the E8 main run itself and is not re-run
quantization: Q4_K_M for every checkpoint, as published by the model owner
host: xbabe4 (Mac Studio, Apple M3 Ultra) CPU only, after E5 and E8 finish; 4 workers x 6 threads; run order qwen3-4b, granite-3.3-8b, qwen3-14b
analysis: Each checkpoint is analysed separately with E8's endpoints; no pooling across checkpoints.

The capability axis is descriptive: per arm, benign utility and attack success are plotted against checkpoint with 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals; no trend test is run (three to four checkpoints, two families).
Granite is a different family at the Qwen3-8B size, not a point on the Qwen size axis.
disclosures: Thinking is disabled for Qwen3; Granite 3.3 has no thinking mode in this template.
Progent policies are generated by the same checkpoint in every run.
A checkpoint whose download hash does not match is not run; the plan is not edited to fit.

amendments.what: base plan updated to E8 Amendment 1 (uniform denial feedback, corrected mediation text, abort handling); per-checkpoint plans regenerated mechanically; no E2 data existed
